headline.headline: ABBOTT EARNS JIMMY V AWARD, A STANDING OVATION DECADES IN THE MAKING
headline.deck: One-handed pitcher's life story moves ESPYS crowd to its feet in Los Angeles
headline.body:
Jim Abbott, the pitcher who spent his entire career throwing at the highest level of professional baseball with one hand, received the Jimmy V Award for Perseverance at the 2026 ESPYS on Wednesday night, drawing one of the evening's loudest and longest ovations. Abbott, who was born without a right hand, reached the major leagues in 1989 and threw a no-hitter for the New York Yankees against the Cleveland Indians in 1993, a moment that remains one of baseball's most enduring stories of human will. The award, named for North Carolina State basketball coach Jim Valvano, who delivered his legendary 'don't give up, don't ever give up' speech while battling cancer in 1993, is given annually to a figure in sports whose perseverance through adversity serves as an inspiration.

Abbott's selection reunites two of 1993's most powerful sports narratives under a single spotlight. Valvano died of cancer just eight weeks after that ESPYS speech. Abbott threw his no-hitter four months later. The symmetry was not lost on the crowd at the ceremony in Los Angeles, where Abbott accepted the award and addressed a room filled with some of the most decorated athletes in American sports.

The Jimmy V Award has been presented since 1993 and has gone to figures ranging from cancer survivors to athletes who overcame catastrophic injury. Abbott's selection this year recognizes not merely a career but a proof of concept, the demonstration that physical difference need not define the ceiling of athletic achievement. For a generation of young athletes with disabilities, Abbott's career remains the loudest argument that sport, at its best, makes no exceptions for the size of a person's heart.

secondary.headline: PERFETTI LOCKS IN WITH JETS, ZEGRAS TOPS FLYERS' BOOKS AS NHL SPENDING ROLLS ON
secondary.deck: Winnipeg and Philadelphia each secure core forwards to multi-year pacts this week
secondary.body:
The NHL's summer spending activity claimed two more significant names on Wednesday as the Winnipeg Jets and center Cole Perfetti agreed to a five-year, $30 million contract, averting salary arbitration and keeping one of the franchise's brightest young pieces off the open market. Perfetti, 23, has developed into a reliable offensive contributor for Winnipeg and the deal, worth $6 million per season, reflects the organization's belief that he is a building block rather than a bridge player. The agreement was first reported Wednesday and confirmed by a source with knowledge of the negotiations.

In Philadelphia, the Flyers made forward Trevor Zegras their highest-paid player by signing him to a four-year contract with an average annual value of $9.125 million. Zegras, the former Anaheim Duck known for his creativity and highlight-reel assists, now carries the largest cap number on a Flyers roster that is in the middle of a rebuild. With Matthew Tkachuk separately weighing in this week on the Florida Panthers goaltending situation, calling Jacob Markstrom the right heir to Sergei Bobrovsky, the league's second round of playoffs is running alongside a busy front-office calendar that will reshape rosters well before October.

secondary.headline: GARRETT TAKES HOME ESPYS HARDWARE, KAMARA REWORKS DEAL TO STAY IN NEW ORLEANS
secondary.deck: Cleveland pass rusher honored for record-breaking 2025 season as Saints keep veteran back
secondary.body:
Myles Garrett of the Cleveland Browns won the Best Record-Breaking Performance award at the 2026 ESPYS on Wednesday night, recognition for a 2025 regular season in which the defensive end put together one of the most dominant pass-rushing campaigns in NFL history. Garrett's award added to what has been a remarkable stretch for the Browns' franchise cornerstone, whose sack total during the 2025 season drew comparisons to the all-time single-season records set by Michael Strahan and the marks approached by T.J. Watt. The ESPYS, held in Los Angeles, also saw Jalen Brunson and A'ja Wilson among the night's other honorees.

Separately, the New Orleans Saints announced that running back Alvin Kamara has agreed to a reworked contract that will keep him in New Orleans for the 2026 season. Kamara, a five-time Pro Bowl selection, had been a subject of offseason uncertainty after his original deal created cap complications for the Saints. The restructured agreement preserves his place in an offense that has leaned heavily on his versatility as both a runner and a receiver out of the backfield. New Orleans begins training camp later this summer with Kamara now locked in as the focal point of the ground game.

secondary.headline: DODGERS TO HONOR PAGES' GAME 7 CATCH WITH BOBBLEHEAD GIVEAWAY
secondary.deck: Los Angeles celebrates one of the most unconventional defensive plays in recent postseason memory
secondary.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers announced this week that an upcoming home game will feature a bobblehead giveaway paying tribute to the remarkable catch made by outfielder Andy Pages in Game 7 of a recent postseason series, a play the organization described as one of the more unconventional and greatest catches in franchise memory. The Dodgers have a long tradition of commemorating signature moments through promotional nights, and the decision to immortalize Pages' catch in bobblehead form signals how deeply the play resonated with the organization and its fanbase. Pages, an outfielder who came up through the Dodgers system, delivered the moment at one of the highest-pressure junctures in baseball.

The giveaway adds to a summer calendar that finds the Dodgers operating as one of the National League's premier franchises while also nurturing a culture of celebrating the players who define their recent championship runs. The Mets arrive in Philadelphia on Thursday for a three-game series against the second-place Phillies, a matchup that will carry its own stakes in the NL East standings. But in Los Angeles, the attention this week turned briefly backward, toward a catch that stopped a crowd cold and turned a postseason game on its axis.

column.headline: JIM ABBOTT DESERVED THIS NIGHT THIRTY YEARS AGO AND DESERVES IT NOW
column.body:
There are awards that feel like paperwork and there are awards that feel like the room exhaling something it has held for thirty years. The Jimmy V Award for Perseverance going to Jim Abbott on Wednesday night at the ESPYS felt like the second kind. Abbott never asked for sympathy during his playing days, never accepted reduced expectations, and never let the camera linger on his right arm long enough for the story to become anything other than baseball. That discipline was its own form of courage, and it is the kind that tends to go unrewarded in real time because it looks, from the outside, like normalcy.

The parallel between Abbott and Valvano is one of those coincidences that sports occasionally produces and then never fully explains. Two men, 1993, refusing to let physical limitation write the final sentence. Valvano died fighting. Abbott threw a no-hitter on a Tuesday afternoon in Yankee Stadium and ran off the mound like a man who had always known it was possible. Honoring Abbott with this award does not close anything. It opens the door a little wider for the next kid who is told the thing he wants to do is not designed for someone built like him.

story.headline: PHILLIES LOOK TO EXTEND NL EAST GRIP AS METS COME TO TOWN FOR THREE-GAME SET
story.deck: Philadelphia hosts struggling New York in a series that could tighten the division race.
story.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies, sitting second in the NL East at 54-43, open a critical three-game home series Thursday against the skidding New York Mets, who have tumbled to fifth place in the division with a 40-57 record. The 14-game gap between the clubs tells most of the story, but Phillies manager Rob Thomson knows better than to take any series against a division rival lightly, particularly one that can shake up playoff positioning down the stretch.

Philadelphia has been one of the National League's steadier clubs in 2026, riding the arms of Zack Wheeler and Ranger Suarez while Bryce Harper continues to anchor one of the more dangerous lineups in the senior circuit. The Mets, meanwhile, have struggled to stay healthy and consistent, with their rotation failing to deliver the kind of depth the front office envisioned when spring training broke. New York will need a sweep just to begin clawing back into relevance in the East.

The series opens Thursday evening at Citizens Bank Park, where the Phillies have played well in front of their passionate South Philly faithful all season. For Philadelphia, these three games represent a chance to pad the cushion on the division leaders and build momentum heading toward the trade deadline. For the Mets, it is quite simply a chance to prove the second half of 2026 will look nothing like the first.

story.headline: ANUNOBY STEALS THE SHOW AT THE ESPYS, TAKES HOME 'BEST PLAY' HONOR
story.deck: The Knicks forward's jaw-dropping defensive gem earns top honors at Hollywood ceremony.
story.body:
LOS ANGELES — OG Anunoby walked away from Wednesday night's ESPY Awards at Dolby Theatre with the sport's most coveted highlight honor, claiming the 'Best Play' award for a defensive sequence that left the basketball world breathless during the 2025-26 season. The New York Knicks forward, whose combination of length, instincts and explosiveness has made him one of the premier two-way players in the league, accepted the award before a star-studded audience packed with professional athletes from across the sporting landscape.

The ceremony provided its own memorable moment when mentalist performer Oz the Mentalist delivered a stunning act that used unsuspecting ESPY attendees as participants, drawing gasps and laughter from the crowd in equal measure. Several NBA players seated in the audience were among those caught off guard by the illusionist's uncanny demonstrations, adding a touch of showbiz spectacle to the annual celebration of athletic excellence.

Anunoby's victory at the ESPYs underscores a remarkable rise for the 28-year-old, who has transformed himself from a promising role player in Toronto into a cornerstone of New York's championship ambitions. The award now sits alongside a growing collection of accolades for a player many around the league consider the most complete defender of his generation. Knicks fans, already energized heading into next season, had yet another reason to celebrate Thursday morning.

story.headline: ZEGRAS TOPS FLYERS' PAYROLL AS NHL SUMMER SPENDING SPREE ROLLS ON
story.deck: Philadelphia locks up electric center while Jets, Devils and Hurricanes also make headlines.
story.body:
The Philadelphia Flyers made Trevor Zegras their highest-paid player Wednesday, announcing a four-year contract extension worth $9.125 million per season. The 24-year-old center, whose jaw-dropping behind-the-net passes and lacrosse-style goals made him one of the most electric players in the league during his Anaheim days, now carries the burden and the banner of a Flyers franchise desperately hunting respectability in the Eastern Conference. Philadelphia is betting that Zegras, healthy and hungry, can be the franchise centerpiece the organization has lacked since the Claude Giroux era.

In Winnipeg, the Jets avoided what could have been an ugly arbitration hearing by locking up center Cole Perfetti to a five-year, $30 million deal, keeping one of the league's most promising young pivots off the open market. Meanwhile in Newark, the Devils added muscle and experience up front by signing veteran power forward Anthony Mantha to a two-year contract worth $9.5 million, giving New Jersey another physical presence alongside Jack Hughes and Nico Hischier as the club pushes to climb back into Stanley Cup contention.

On the league calendar front, the NHL announced that the champion Carolina Hurricanes will raise their second Stanley Cup banner on Sept. 29 before hosting the Florida Panthers in the season opener, a rematch of two fierce Eastern Conference rivals. Florida captain Matthew Tkachuk also weighed in on the Panthers' goaltending transition Wednesday, saying new netminder Jacob Markstrom is the ideal successor to Sergei Bobrovsky between the pipes. Tkachuk's endorsement carries weight in a locker room that knows better than most what it takes to win deep into June.

story.headline: VETERANS FIND NEW HOMES AS NFL FREE AGENCY FRENZY RESHAPES ROSTERS AHEAD OF TRAINING CAMP
story.deck: Big names on the move as teams retool rosters following February's Super Bowl LX.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has hit full stride, with front offices across the league finalizing rosters before training camps open in late July. The Dallas Cowboys made the most aggressive move of the week, agreeing to terms with veteran linebacker Roquan Smith on a three-year deal worth $54 million, signaling a major philosophical shift toward defensive investment under new head coach Mike Vrabel, who left New England to take the job in March. The Cowboys finished 2025 with the league's 28th-ranked defense, and ownership made clear that patching those holes was the top priority entering the new league year.

Meanwhile, the Chicago Bears continued their post-draft makeover by trading wide receiver DJ Moore to the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick and a veteran offensive lineman. Bears general manager Ryan Poles confirmed the deal late Wednesday, noting that the team's offensive rebuild around second-year quarterback Caleb Williams would center on younger, cheaper weapons rather than holdover veterans. Pittsburgh, desperate for proven receiving talent after a disappointing 2025 campaign, expects Moore to slot immediately into the starting lineup alongside emerging tight end Sam LaPorta, acquired from Detroit in a separate deal last month.

NFL draft analysts continued dissecting April's seven-round selection meeting, with the consensus view hardening that the Las Vegas Raiders landed the class's top prospect by taking Georgia edge rusher Mykel Williams third overall. Raiders defensive coordinator Patrick Graham told reporters Tuesday that Williams has exceeded expectations in informal workouts, displaying pass-rush technique rarely seen from a player his age. Across the league, rookie minicamp footage has fueled early optimism in several rebuilding cities, with the Carolina Panthers and New York Giants both generating buzz around their first-round quarterbacks as the long wait for training camp slowly ticks down.
